messages:
Anya (Product Design): dropped a couple quick mocks + a short writeup of a change I'm proposing for the compare view 12 trying to reduce left-rail clutter and make version pinning feel like a persistent compare context instead of a tiny per-row toggle. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/compare-rail-proposals :eyes: Sam (PM): can you summarize the user problem in one line? who uses pinning now and what failure are we seeing? Anya (Product Design): TL;DR: advanced users often maintain 4-8 pinned versions; current UI mixes these with filter controls so scanning suffers. users treat the pin like it should create a persistent "compare lane" but the icon today reads like a one-off row action. goal: establish a dedicated lane for pinned versions, reduce filter noise, and make pin persistence clear across navigation. Rachel (Design): lane metaphor reads well. immediate reaction: collapsed rail in the mock takes too much space when toggled. can we show a thin collapsed rail with just compact badges/counts? full-width collapse creates jarring layout shifts. :thinking: Leo (Frontend): we have a collapsed-rail pattern we can reuse. animating width causes table reflow which hurts perceived perf. overlay with absolute positioning avoids reflow but needs careful z-index and focus handling. Kai (Eng): overlay sounds right. watch out for stacking context with tooltips and select dropdowns; also keyboard focus management will need a proper trap/untrap. Alex (A11y): overlay/trap is fine. ensure the rail toggle is keyboard operable and exposes aria-expanded. when a pin changes, announce via aria-live="polite". example:
Filters collapsed
Anya (Product Design): yes, will add accessibility notes. also thinking about clearer copy: change tooltip from icon-only "pin" to "Pin to compare" and hover text "Keep this version in your compare lane". reduces ambiguity. Sam (PM): +1. Julie, any analytics on pin usage vs expansion-only? Julie (Data): quick look: ~12% of compare sessions touch the pin control; only ~4% maintain >1 pinned after 30s. discoverability OK, but retention low. making pins persistent across nav likely increases retention. i can add events: pin.create, pin.remove, pin.persisted-session. Leo (Frontend): persistence: localStorage is easiest for initial rollout; server-side per-org later if we need cross-device. Sam (PM): product decision: start with localStorage, track signals, then prioritize server persist for orgs. Anya (Product Design): UX question: when multiple versions are pinned, show them as chips or mini-tabs? current mock uses chips but they compress poorly once you have several. Rachel (Design): mini-tabs scale better for quick switching; chips are nice for glanceable metadata. hybrid idea: tabs for first 4 pins, overflow menu for extras showing chips with metadata. Alex (A11y): tabs have semantic accessibility benefits. if we emulate tabs with buttons, add role="tablist" and role="tab" plus aria-selected. keyboard arrow navigation expected for tablists. Kai (Eng): implementation note: tablist changes focus behavior; we should prototype to ensure screen reader users switching between table content and tabs isn't confusing. Anya (Product Design): next: performance badges. today we show p95 latency and cost/token inline which looks noisy. proposal: collapse badges to icon-only summary; on hover/tap show the full metrics in a small flyout. Rachel (Design): icon-only OK for desktop hover. for touch, make the chip tappable to open a flyout. ensure the tap target meets 44px guideline. Leo (Frontend): tooltips + flyouts doable. we should lazy-load metric values when the flyout opens to avoid extra payload on list render. Julie (Data): metrics endpoint exists for per-model metrics. lazy-load is fine; we can return cached values for short durations to avoid spikes. Sam (PM): can we commit to shipping collapsed rail, pin lane, and icon-only badges next sprint? Kai (Eng): estimate ~2w dev + 3d QA. server-side pin persistence out of scope for this sprint. Anya (Product Design): I'll update Figma with: (1) thin collapsed rail state with counts, (2) pin lane using tabs + overflow, (3) icon-only badges with flyout pattern, (4) copy updates including "Pin to compare" and touch microcopy. will ping @Leo and @Alex for dev/a11y review once done. Rachel (Design): microcopy nit: prefer sentence case "Pin to compare" (not Title Case) for consistency with console copy. Alex (A11y): also: visible focus styles for pinned items. low-contrast outlines fail WCAG; use a focus stroke with >= 3:1 contrast. Leo (Frontend): will add CSS var --focus-stroke and enforce contrast check. ci-bot: staging build scheduled 2026-04-01T06:00Z for UI experiment. :rocket: Sam (PM): thanks all. Anya, drop updated figma link here and I'll add to sprint backlog. :thumbsup:
